Talk to Gladys from [Rocket.Chat](https://www.rocket.chat), the open-source team chat you can host
yourself, the way the Telegram bot of Gladys works: ask a question, run a scene, receive the messages of
Gladys in a direct message. The integration also posts in Rocket.Chat channels from your scenes, and starts
scenes when a message or a command such as `!lights off` is written in a channel it watches. It uses a bot
account of your Rocket.Chat server, on the local network or on the Internet.

> **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome.** The integration was tested against a real
> Rocket.Chat server (8.9, in Docker), but not inside a real Gladys nor with every Rocket.Chat client.
> Please report what works and what does not in the
> [issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-rocketchat/issues) or on the
> [Gladys forum](https://community.gladysassistant.com).

## What you need

- Gladys Assistant **5.1.0** or later.
- A Rocket.Chat server Gladys can reach (tested with 8.9; sending images needs 6.8 or later), and an
  administrator account to create the bot.
- A **user for the bot**, with a personal access token. Do not use your personal account: the bot answers
  in its name.
- The username of each person allowed to talk to the bot, such as `alice`.

## Set up

1. In Rocket.Chat, **Administration → Users → New user**: a username such as `gladys`, an email and a
   password, the roles **bot** and **user**.
2. Log in to Rocket.Chat as this user, **Profile → Personal access tokens**: give a name, tick **Ignore
   two-factor authentication**, click **Add**. Copy the **token** and the **user id** shown once.
3. In Gladys, **Integrations → Rocket.Chat → Configuration**:
   - **Server address**: the address of Rocket.Chat as in the browser, for example
     `https://chat.example.org` or `http://192.168.1.20:3000`.
   - **User id of the bot** and **Personal access token**: the two values of step 2.
   - **Allowed people**: the usernames the bot listens to, separated by commas (`alice, bob`), written as
     in Rocket.Chat: the case matters. **Empty, the bot answers nobody**: it ignores the messages of
     everyone who is not in this list.
   - **Watched channels**: the channels whose messages start scenes, written `#name` (the address
     `https://chat.example.org/channel/garage` or the id of the channel are accepted too), separated by
     commas. The bot joins the public channels by itself; add it to the private ones first.
   - **Command prefix**: `!` by default (`/` is taken by the slash commands of Rocket.Chat).
   - **Language of the bot**: the language of what the bot writes before a person is linked.
4. Click **Test the connection**: the report gives the account of the bot, the watched channels it joined
   and the allowed people it found. The connection status of the page says it too, and names a channel or
   a person that was not found.

### Link your Rocket.Chat account to talk to Gladys

Each Gladys user who wants to talk to Gladys from Rocket.Chat does it once:

1. In Gladys, **Integrations → Rocket.Chat → Configuration**, block "Link my account": click **Generate a
   link code**.
2. In Rocket.Chat, open a **direct message** with the bot (the pencil icon **Create new → Direct
   message**, then its username) and send it the code (8 characters). The bot confirms: your Rocket.Chat
   account is linked to your Gladys user. You can unlink it from the same block.

## What the bot does

- **In a direct message** with an allowed person: it passes the messages to Gladys, with the authority of
  the linked Gladys user, exactly like the Telegram bot: "What is the temperature in the living room?",
  "Turn off the lights". The answers of Gladys come back in this direct message, Markdown rendered by
  Rocket.Chat. The messages Gladys sends to you (the **Send Message** scene action, the system messages)
  arrive there too, even before any conversation. A camera image sent by a scene arrives as an image.
- **In a watched channel**: every message of an allowed person starts the **Rocket.Chat message received**
  trigger, and a message starting with the prefix also starts **Rocket.Chat command received**. The bot
  never answers there by itself: what happens is up to your scenes.
- **In any other room** (a channel that is not watched, a direct message with several people): it stays
  silent. Gladys never answers where others can read.
- **What it ignores**: everyone who is not an allowed person, its own messages (a scene that posts in a
  watched channel never starts itself again), the messages of incoming webhooks and apps (even when they
  post in the name of an allowed person), the system messages ("joined the channel"), edits, and the
  messages older than 5 minutes when it reads them (a "!open garage" from two hours ago does not run now).
- **After a cut** (a restart of the server, of Gladys, a network blip): it reconnects by itself, and reads
  back the messages of the watched channels and of the direct messages posted in the last 5 minutes.

## Dashboard

The **Rocket.Chat** widget shows whether the bot is connected, its account, the watched channels it is in,
the last 5 messages received in the watched channels (author, text, date) and a **Test the connection**
button. The direct messages with Gladys are never shown: everyone who sees the dashboard sees the widget.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Rocket.Chat message received**: an allowed person wrote in a watched channel. Filters (empty = any):
  **Channel** (written as in the configuration, for example `#garage`) and **Sender** (the username,
  without `@`: `alice`). Variables: Message, Sender, Channel, Channel id.
- **Rocket.Chat command received**: an allowed person wrote a command in a watched channel: the prefix,
  then a word, then optional arguments, for example `!lights off kitchen`. Filter **Command**: the word
  **without the prefix, in lower case** (`lights`); and Channel, Sender. Variables: Command (`lights`),
  Arguments (`off kitchen`), Message, Sender, Channel, Channel id. The same message also starts
  **Rocket.Chat message received**.
- **Rocket.Chat connection lost**: the bot cannot reach the server any more, for a minute, or its token is
  refused. Variable: Error. Started once, until the connection comes back.
- **Rocket.Chat connection restored**: the bot reaches the server again after a lost connection. Variable:
  Bot account (username).

### Actions

- **Send a Rocket.Chat message**: posts a message in a channel (`#name`, its address or its id), or to a
  person in a direct message (`@alice`). The message accepts the scene variables and the Markdown of
  Rocket.Chat (`**bold**`, `_italic_`, lists, links, `@here`). A public channel takes the message even if
  the bot is not in it; a private channel only if the bot is a member. Results: Sent (yes/no), Message id,
  Error. A failed message does not stop the scene: test **Sent** with a condition if needed.

To write to one Gladys user, the **Send Message** action of Gladys also works: it reaches their linked
Rocket.Chat account.

### Scene ideas

- **Garage by command**: trigger **Rocket.Chat command received**, command `garage`, channel `#garage`;
  then a condition on the variable Arguments equal to `close`, and the action that closes the garage.
- **Washing machine done**: when the power of the washing machine plug drops, **Send a Rocket.Chat
  message** to `#family`: "The washing machine is done @here".
- **Alert when the bot is cut off**: trigger **Rocket.Chat connection lost**, then a notification through
  another channel (Gotify, ntfy, SMS) with the Error variable.

## Troubleshooting

- **"no Rocket.Chat server at this address"**: use the address you open Rocket.Chat with in a browser,
  without `/home` nor a channel. `https://<address>/api/info` must answer `{"version":…,"success":true}`.
- **"user id or access token refused"**: the token was removed, the user id is not the one of the token,
  or the bot account was deactivated. Create a new token in **Profile → Personal access tokens**.
- **A watched channel is not joined**: the status of the page and the test name it. Check the name of the
  channel, add the bot to it if it is private, then save the configuration again.
- **The bot does not answer me**: is your username in **Allowed people**, written exactly, with the same
  case? Do you write to it in a direct message with the bot alone? Is your account linked (the bot then
  gives you the instructions)?
- **A command does not start the scene**: the Command filter is the word without the prefix, in lower
  case: `lights`, not `!Lights`.
- **Behind a reverse proxy**, the WebSocket (`/websocket`) must be forwarded too, as for the Rocket.Chat
  apps.
- More details in the logs of the integration with `LOG_LEVEL=debug`.

## Limits

- A person linked to Gladys can do from Rocket.Chat everything their Gladys user can do: keep the list of
  allowed people short, and keep the token of the bot secret.
- One bot account per Gladys. The bot reads the messages over the real-time API of Rocket.Chat (DDP over
  the WebSocket): a command takes effect in about a second. Messages missed during a cut longer than 5
  minutes are skipped.
- Files, images and voice messages sent to the bot are ignored; only text counts. Threads are read as
  ordinary messages, and the answers of Gladys are not posted in the thread.
- A message holds 5000 characters by default (setting **Message → Maximum allowed message size**): a
  longer answer of Gladys is cut. The bot role is exempt from the API rate limits of the server.
- Not affiliated with Rocket.Chat Technologies Corp. Rocket.Chat is a trademark of Rocket.Chat
  Technologies Corp.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Rocket.Chat asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Create a user for the bot in Rocket.Chat (Administration → Users, role bot), log in with it, create a personal access token (Profile → Personal access tokens) and copy the token and the user id. Then write to it in a direct message. |
| Server address | `string` | Yes | The address of your Rocket.Chat, as in the browser, e.g. https:\/\/chat.example.org or http:\/\/192.168.1.20:3000. |
| User id of the bot | `string` | Yes | Shown next to the token when you create it (17 or 24 characters). |
| Personal access token | `secret` | No | The personal access token of the bot account (tick “Ignore two-factor authentication” when you create it). |
| Allowed people | `string` | No | Usernames the bot listens to, separated by commas, as written in Rocket.Chat (case matters), e.g. alice, bob. Empty: the bot answers nobody. |
| Watched channels | `string` | No | Channels whose messages trigger scenes, as #name, by address or by id, separated by commas. The bot joins public channels; add it to private ones. |
| Command prefix | `string` | No | A message starting with it is a command, e.g. !lights off. One to three characters. |
| Language of the bot | `select` | No | Language of what the bot writes before a person is linked, and of the reports. |

## How to install Rocket.Chat in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Rocket.Chat appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-rocketchat:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-rocketchat](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-rocketchat).

Rocket.Chat requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Rocket.Chat is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
